title: CPF employer guide for Singapore businesses: What finance leaders need to know
summary: Understand CPF employer requirements in Singapore, from employee eligibility and wage classifications to CPF calculations, ceilings, and payroll changes
body_markdown:
## What is CPF


The Central Provident Fund is Singapore’s mandatory social security scheme, supporting employees’ healthcare, housing, and retirement. Both employees and employers must contribute to CPF, so finance leaders who understand these regulations can keep payroll accurate and avoid any compliance issues.


The CPF system allocates members’ savings across four accounts:


- **Ordinary Account (OA):** Supports savings for housing, education, and other approved needs


- **Special Account (SA):** Holds savings primarily intended for retirement


- **MediSave Account (MA):** Covers healthcare expenses and approved medical insurance


- **Retirement Account (RA):** Created at 55 to hold savings set aside for retirement


### Who and what are subject to CPF


CPF employer requirements do not apply to all your employees. The CPF Singapore framework clearly defines which employees fall under these laws. Therefore, the first step for finance leaders is to establish which employees require CPF contributions. These generally include: ****


- **Singapore citizens** employed in Singapore


- **Singapore Permanent Residents (SPRs)** employed in Singapore


The applicable CPF rates can vary based on an employee’s age, so finance teams should keep up with CPF changes regularly.


But identifying the CPF-eligible portion of your workforce is only step one. Next, you’ll need to determine which parts of each employee’s remuneration is subject to CPF. The wages covered by CPF are broadly classified into Ordinary Wage (OW) and Additional Wage (AW).

## Understanding CPF contributions


Payments towards an employee’s CPF come from both the employee and their employer. While the employer processes both payments, each is handled differently.


- **Employee contribution:** All eligible employees must contribute towards their CPF payments. A percentage is deducted from their wage by the employer. Then the employer submits this amount directly to the CPF Board without any action from the employee.[Different rates](https://aspireapp.com/blog/employee-cpf-contribution-singapore) apply depending on the employee’s age.


- **Employer contribution:** In addition to the employee’s contribution, as an employer, you have your own CPF liabilities for each employee. This is an added cost to your business on top of the wages you’re already paying your employee.


Finance teams must calculate both CPF contributions and submit them by the last day of the calendar month. Enforcement action may apply if payment is not made by the[14th of the following month](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/employer/making-cpf-contributions) , or the next working day if the 14th falls on a weekend or public holiday. Late payment interest is charged at 1.5% per month from the day after the due date, subject to a minimum of SGD $5.


## When employee changes affect CPF


Changes in an employee’s age, residency status, salary, or employment situation all affect how their CPF is calculated. As a finance leader, you must stay on top of these details to keep payroll accurate and ensure your CPF employer obligations remain compliant.


These changes can happen at any point during the year, so finance teams cannot rely solely on quarterly or annual payroll reviews to catch them. Instead, your payroll process should have clear instructions on what happens when an employee's circumstances change.


Some major changes that your finance team needs predefined processes for are:


- [Employee becomes a Singapore Citizen](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/service/article/what-should-i-do-if-there-is-a-change-in-employee-s-particulars) **:** When an employee receives their new Singapore Identity Card, they will receive a new CPF account linked to the new identity-card number. Pay CPF Singapore contributions into the new account and ask the employee to contact the CPF Board to merge their previous CPF employer account with the new one, where applicable.


- **Employee becomes a Singapore PR:** Apply the[graduated CPF payment rates](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/content/dam/web/employer/employer-obligations/documents/CPFcontributionratesfrom1Jan2026.pdf) for the first two years of their PR status, with full contribution rates applying from the third year onwards.


- **Employee moves into a new age band:** The revised contribution rate applies from the first day of the month following the month in which the employee's birthday falls.


- **Employee renounces Singapore Citizen/SPR status:** For OW, CPF contributions are required only for the portion earned up to the date the employee renounces their status. For AW, CPF applies only if the AW is payable before the renunciation takes effect. AW payable on or after the renunciation date does not attract CPF.


- **Employee leaves the company:** Before removing the employee from your payroll records, tick the checkbox beside their employee record in CPF EZPay and select Delete Employee Record.


### CPF changes 2026


Rules around CPF contributions, CPF ceilings, and CPF caps can change from year to year. It is imperative for finance leaders and their teams to stay updated on these changes. There are 2 major CPF changes 2026:


- **Ordinary Wage ceiling increased to SGD $8000:** Effective 1 January 2026, the monthly OW ceiling increased from SGD $7400 to SGD $8000. This means that up to SGD $8000 of an employee’s monthly OW can be subject to CPF contributions.


- **Higher CPF rates for senior workers:** From 1 January 2026, contribution rates for employees in the 55-60 and 60-65 age bands increased from 32.5% to 34% and 23.5% to 25% respectively.


## How to calculate CPF contributions


Finance leaders should understand how both employee and employer CPF is calculated, but the[CPF Board's online calculator](http://cpf.gov.sg/employer/tools-and-services/calculators/cpf-contribution-calculator) can help you determine the correct contributions for each employee.


### Step 1. Determine if the employee is eligible


- Confirm employee’s citizenship and PR status


- If the employee is a PR, confirm whether they are in their first, second, or third year onwards of their PR


- Check whether any recent change in the employee's status affects the CPF treatment


### Step 2. Determine the employee’s age band


- Identify the applicable employee age band


- Check if employee recently moved to a new age band


- Apply the relevant[CPF contribution rates](https://help.aspireapp.com/sg/en/articles/10798774-calculating-salaries-cpf-contributions)


### Step 3. Determine the employee’s Total Wage (TW)


- Confirm the employee’s OW and AW


- Add the OW and AW to determine the employee’s TW


- Check whether any payments should be excluded because they do not constitute wages for CPF purposes


### Step 4. Apply the CPF ceilings


- Apply the monthly OW ceiling to the employee’s OW


- Calculate the employee's applicable AW ceiling, taking into account their OW for the calendar year


- Check the employee's cumulative OW when calculating CPF on AW


- Determine the portion of OW and AW that is subject to CPF after applying the respective ceilings


### Step 5. Calculate the contributions using the correct rates


- Apply the applicable CPF employer and employee rates to the CPF-payable wages


- Calculate the employee's share to be deducted from their salary


- Calculate the employer's share as an additional payroll cost


- Add both shares to determine the total CPF amount payable

## Building reliable CPF processes


1. Integrate HR changes directly into payroll


Connect relevant HR updates directly with your payroll process. This ensures that changes to an employee’s citizenship, PR status, age, salary, or employment status automatically trigger a CPF review.


Define which HR changes need to reach payroll and how quickly they need to be attended. This reduces reliance on manual communication to ensure CPF caps, CPF ceilings, and CPF contributions are accurately calculated from the correct effective date.


1. Flag updated and unusual changes before payroll closes


Create a review process that flags payments or employee changes that could require different CPF treatment. This can include bonuses, commissions, allowances, post-termination payments, or employees moving into a new age band. Review these changes before payroll closes so your team has time to confirm the correct treatment and make any necessary adjustments before submitting the month's CPF employer payment.


1. Review CPF treatment when introducing new pay components


Before introducing a new compensation structure, determine its place in the CPF framework. New allowances, incentives, commission structures, or bonus schemes should be classified correctly and have their CPF treatment confirmed before they are added to payroll.


1. Document CPF-related processes clearly


Maintain clear documentation for your CPF-related payroll processes. Include comprehensive information like ownership, what information needs to be checked, when changes take effect, and what steps to follow for different employee scenarios. Keep these instructions accessible to both finance and payroll teams and update them when CPF rules change.


## Common CPF mistakes


### Using outdated employee information


Changes in employee information must be reflected immediately and accurately across your payroll systems. Using outdated information can result in incorrect employer CPF contributions.


### Misclassifying wage types


CPF calculations for OWs and AWs are treated differently. Finance teams should confirm and review the classifications of each payment type before processing their CPF employer rates.


### Declaring wages based on the CPF ceiling


When submitting CPF, employers should declare the employee's actual wages. Often, employers misrepresent the employee’s wages according to the CPF ceiling.

## Simplifying CPF management


Managing CPF manually can become increasingly difficult as your workforce grows. The right payroll tools can automate repetitive calculations and payment processes, making CPF part of your regular payroll workflow rather than a separate task.


Connected payroll systems can also reduce manual updates across different platforms and help keep employee information aligned with payroll.[Aspire's global payroll](https://aspireapp.com/use-case/payroll) is one such platform, bringing salary and CPF payments into the same workflow, with local salary payments supported through FAST or GIRO.


With the right processes and tools in place, finance teams can spend less time managing CPF manually and more time focusing on payroll oversight and the wider finance function.


## Frequently Asked Questions


1. Which employees are required to contribute to CPF in Singapore?


CPF employer requirements generally apply to Singapore Citizens and Singapore Permanent Residents employed in Singapore. The applicable contribution rates can vary based on factors such as age and PR status.


1. What are the major CPF changes in 2026?


The key CPF changes 2026 include the increase in the monthly OW ceiling from SGD $7400 to SGD $8000 and higher contribution rates for certain senior-worker age bands. Finance teams should ensure their payroll processes reflect the latest requirements.


1. How is the employer CPF contribution calculated?


The employer CPF contribution is calculated by applying the applicable employer rate to the employee's CPF-payable wages after considering the relevant wage ceilings. The employee's share is calculated separately and deducted from their salary.


1. When do employers need to pay CPF?


Employers must submit CPF contributions by the last day of the calendar month. Finance teams should also account for the applicable enforcement timeline and ensure payments are submitted promptly.


1. What should employers do when CPF requirements change during the year?


Finance teams should have processes for identifying changes such as a new age band, changes in citizenship or PR status, salary adjustments and new types of remuneration. These changes should trigger a review of the employee's CPF treatment.
